reviewType: independent AI re-lemma and lesson-feasibility gate
scope: Five missed-teachable hold candidates 2341,2343,2418,2423,2435 and dependent duplicates 2377,2379
method: Applied SOP P79–P85 to exact source examples and existing canonical briefs; designed source-matching but constrained target patterns, tested each against all Books 10–16 source examples and positive/negative controls, compared nearest prior owners, then outlined seven distinct learner actions. Recommendations do not edit decisions.

candidates.sourceExample: He does more than recite the part; he inhabits it.
candidates.normalizedLemma: inhabit a role / inhabit a part
candidates.learnerDecision: Judge whether an actor fully embodies a role, beyond accurately reciting its lines.
candidates.canonicalComparison: No existing owner teaches this acting sense. Canonical index keyword scan found none; original theatre criticism attests inhabit the part. The source pronoun is licensed only by the immediately preceding the part, so its detector branch is exact-context lookbehind rather than global inhabit it.
sevenStepFeasibility: Infer full embodiment from listening to acting feedback.
Give four valid replies to a director question; only golden uses target.
Select a concrete actor-embodiment scene.
Distinguish embodiment from memorising lines.
Continue a director–actor exchange naturally.
Hear and say a target-bearing model about a role.
Write in a changed school-play context with answer-derived glossary.

candidates.sourceExample: Her modest interviews are brief, but the performance usually does the talking.
candidates.sourceTargetMatch: the performance usually does the talking
negative: He does the talking for the team.
positive: Let the results do the talking.
candidates.learnerDecision: Let work or results provide convincing evidence without relying on self-promotion or a verbal claim.
candidates.canonicalComparison: No prior owner teaches the do-the-talking personification. Inanimate evidence-subject whitelist prevents ordinary person-does-the-talking literal readings; source subject performance is included.
sevenStepFeasibility: Infer evidence-through-work from a performance model.
Give four valid responses about brief interviews; golden uses target.
Choose a work/result scene rather than a speech scene.
Distinguish outcomes proving merit from merely staying silent.
Continue a conversation about modest self-presentation.
Hear and say a model about results doing the talking.
Write in a changed charity-results context with exact answer-derived glossary.

candidates.sourceExample: The investigator slowly untangles the lies.
negative: The lies unravelled on their own.
candidates.learnerDecision: Describe actively clarifying how several deceptive claims fit together, rather than simply detecting one false statement.
candidates.canonicalComparison: No existing untangle owner. Canonical 1425 start to unravel means arrangements lose coherence, the opposite process; Cambridge licenses figurative transitive untangle for a confusing matter. Do not label this a fixed idiom.
sevenStepFeasibility: Infer clarification of intertwined deception.
Give four valid replies to an investigative update; golden uses target.
Choose an evidence-sorting scene.
Distinguish untangling several claims from spotting one lie.
Continue an investigator–colleague exchange.
Hear and say a target-bearing model.
Write in a changed financial-audit context with exact answer-derived glossary.

candidates.sourceExample: The new system will take the heavy lifting out of routine checks.
candidates.sourceTargetMatch: take the heavy lifting out of
candidates.normalizedLemma: take the heavy lifting out of [a task]
negative: Take the heavy lifting off their shoulders.
The team did the heavy lifting.
positive: The system takes the heavy lifting out of daily checks.
Automation took the heavy lifting out of the review.
candidates.learnerDecision: Choose out of a process when the difficult work is removed from that process, versus off people’s shoulders when people are relieved of it.
candidates.canonicalComparison: Meaning overlaps canonical 1376 (take heavy lifting off people’s shoulders) and 252 (do most of the heavy lifting). The new out of [process] argument structure is attested and current owner detectors do not match; decide whether to extend 1376 as a construction family or commission a distinct grammar-focused owner before promotion.
sevenStepFeasibility: Infer workload removal from a process.
Give four valid replies about automation; golden uses target.
Choose a process-simplification scene.
Distinguish out of a task from off someone’s shoulders.
Continue a team-planning exchange.
Hear and say a complete model.
Write in a changed clinic-intake context with exact answer-derived glossary.

candidates.sourceExample: Sorting receipts became a never-ending chore.
negative: She sees it as a chore.
positive: Sorting receipts became a never-ending chore.
These checks feel like never-ending chores.
candidates.learnerDecision: Use the collocation for an unwelcome task that seems not to end, not merely a long finite job or any disliked duty.
candidates.canonicalComparison: Canonical 1123 a never-ending race teaches continual competitive pressure; 1730 see it as a chore teaches viewing an activity as an unwelcome duty. Neither combines apparently endless duration with chore. SOP P79 admits reusable Natural English collocations, but this transparent unit needs a strong seven-step brief to avoid thin exercises.
sevenStepFeasibility: Infer seemingly endless tedious task from a model.
Give four valid replies about an ongoing duty; golden uses target.
Choose a recurring, open-ended chore scene.
Distinguish a long finite task or one disliked duty.
Continue a colleague complaint without exaggerating a finished task.
Hear and say a complete model.
Write in a changed household-admin context with exact answer-derived glossary.
